reason: The cited evidence does not directly address the NbZrTiHfMo system or the role of electronegativity in its plasticity. E1 discusses V effects on lattice distortion and strength in FCC HEAs, not electronegativity or plasticity in BCC alloys. E2 shows Mo alters phases in a different alloy system but does not link electronegativity to plasticity. E3 discusses lattice distortion and dislocation width in general but not electronegativity or V substitution. Thus, the key premises lack specific prior support.
premises: High Mo content increases electronegativity difference in NbZrTiHfMo, reducing plasticity
V has lower electronegativity than Mo, so substituting V for Mo reduces electronegativity gradients
Reduced electronegativity gradients facilitate dislocation motion and enhance plasticity
Preserved lattice distortion from V substitution maintains high strength
V substitution must be low (~5 at%) to avoid diluting lattice distortion and compromising strength
